learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 100 m saved and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Initial 100 east/200 north gave L route 300, straight 224, saved 76. At 200/200 gave 400,283,117. Set asked 300/400: 700,500,200. Home both sliders zero gave all zeros. Restored 300/400 with same result.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 200, derived square root of squared legs, gave about twenty-nine percent saving and flat-ground condition. Said straight side always shorter than sum.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Dashed orthogonal route, solid diagonal, grid and two comparison bars aligned. Brief compilation-time saved chip appeared zero after restore; subsequent full AX and screenshot showed stable 200, matching prose.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete familiar route prediction tests right-triangle distance.

interaction.reason: Two dimensions, symmetric case and zero boundary expose relation reversibly.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects observed distances to squared-leg formula and percentage.

clarity.reason: Line styles, metre units and bars reinforce calculation.

transfer.reason: General formula is supplied within the same route task without a new application.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard dimensions and zero boundary worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Diagonal saves a substantial part of a familiar route.
surprise.evidence: Two hundred of seven hundred metres.

visualExplanation.reason: Route geometry and length bars show the same comparison.

depth.reason: One geometric relation with percentage comparison.

complexity.reason: Easy controls introduce squared distances and square roots.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish summed orthogonal legs from straight Euclidean distance.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Right-triangle squared-leg relation introduced at reveal.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Metres, squared values and square roots.

whyCool: A route map and length bars make the diagonal saving measurable.
caveat: The statement always shorter excludes degenerate zero-leg cases available in controls; at zero/zero equality was observed. Flat-ground assumption explicit.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
